headline: Home Batteries Break US Record During California Heat Wave
meta_description: Home batteries delivered 745 MW to California's grid in a single evening, powering San Francisco and San Jose at peak demand.
summary_short: During California's heat wave, residential batteries set a US record by sending 745 MW to the grid—enough to power two major cities combined.
body:
Home batteries across California set a new US record by delivering 745 megawatts to the electrical grid in a single evening during the state's heat wave. This output proved substantial enough to power every household in San Francisco and San Jose combined at peak demand.

The milestone reflects a quiet shift in how California manages its energy during extreme weather. Rather than relying solely on traditional power plants during sweltering conditions, thousands of households with battery systems—often paired with rooftop solar—acted as a distributed power source when the grid needed it most.

The achievement underscores an emerging reality: as heat waves become more frequent and intense, the combination of home solar and battery storage isn't just a consumer choice anymore. It's becoming critical infrastructure, allowing communities to stabilize their own power supply while reducing strain on centralized systems.
